name: zshdb
why: A step debugger for zsh scripts lets you watch a shell program execute line by line, a useful way into how shells run code.

brief.what_it_is: zshdb is a gdb-like interactive debugger for zsh scripts. You run a zsh script under it and step through execution line by line, setting breakpoints and inspecting state, with gdb-style command syntax. It is a port of the author's bashdb, so many commands match. The documentation index lists version 1.1.3.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says it started as a port of Rocky Bernstein's bash debugger bashdb, so zsh users get the same kind of debugging. The command syntax follows the trepanning debuggers and gdb, so skills carry over to those tools.
brief.install_notes: The README does not give install steps. The documentation index has sections titled 'From a Package' and 'From Source' and 'Invoking the Debugger Initially', but I did not open those pages, so I have no details on them.
brief.standout: It is a shell debugger that follows gdb and trepanning command syntax, so gdb users can use it without learning a new interface. It also has editor and IDE integrations: an Emacs interface through realgud and a Visual Studio Code extension, ZshDebug, by rogalmic.
brief.status: unknown. The README has a CircleCI build badge and a Repology packaging badge, and the docs footer shows copyright 2017, 2019 and 2023, which suggests activity into 2023. I did not see a release date or last-commit date.
brief.caveats: I did not reach the command reference or install pages, so I could not verify commands or options. The README is short and points to external docs and a wiki for details.
quotes: zshdb is gdb-like debugger for zsh scripts. It started as a port of my bash debugger bashdb so the commands used in both are similar.
The command syntax generally follows that of the trepanning debuggers and, more generally, GNU debugger gdb.
An Emacs interface is available via realgud.
